reason: Amino acids and phospholipids are shown supporting protein production and expanding cell membranes, so they fit the growth goal.
expectation: The cell will grow using these materials, preparing for division.

effect: The cell has grown, but its nuclear DNA remains uncopied, so DNA copying is the next part of the goal.
reaction: The before-and-after cutaway clearly separates growth from DNA copying.
reason: DNA nucleotides are the building blocks needed to copy the cell's DNA.
expectation: The growing cell will copy its DNA in preparation for division.

effect: DNA replication is complete; the next goal is to separate the copies and divide the cell.
reaction: The distinct strand styles help distinguish DNA replication from protein production.
reason: The spindle is shown attaching to duplicated chromosomes and extending toward opposite poles, making it the natural next step.
expectation: The spindle will separate the chromosome copies toward opposite poles.

effect: The chromosome sets have separated into two nuclei, but the cell still shares one membrane and cytoplasm.
reaction: The intermediate inset makes the separation clear.
reason: The actin–myosin ring is shown around the cell's equator, where it can constrict to divide the cell.
expectation: The ring will constrict and separate the cell into two daughter cells.

effect: The ring completed cell division, and the repeated pairs connect one division to a growing stem-cell population.
reaction: The closing bridge makes the final separation easy to follow.

mostWorthwhile.text: Separating the copied chromosomes and then dividing the cell was most worthwhile: the two planned cutaways distinguish nuclear separation from division of the cytoplasm.

leastWorthwhile.text: The growth step was relatively predictable, though its planned before-and-after view usefully separates growth from DNA copying.

surprise.text: The final picture extends beyond two daughters to a population retaining cells for further division; that broadened the outcome beyond the immediate split.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary: each supplied piece had a visible role in the sequence. The term “mitotic spindle” itself could benefit from a brief explanation for students unfamiliar with it.

continue.text: I would continue: the sequence made the mechanics of division clear, and I would be curious to see how these cells' descendants take different paths.
